name: Battle of Chancellorsville
kicker: Lee’s great 1863 victory over Hooker · Stonewall Jackson shot by his own men
briefing: In May 1863, Robert E. Lee faced a Union army more than twice the size of his own near a crossroads in the Virginia woods called Chancellorsville. Lee boldly split his army and sent Stonewall Jackson on a secret march around the Union flank, and the surprise attack sent Joseph Hooker’s army reeling. But that night, Jackson was accidentally shot by his own men, and he died eight days later.
answerHtml: Battle of Chancellorsville (do not accept “Battle of the Wilderness” or “Fredericksburg”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: On the night of May 2, 1863, during this battle, soldiers of the 18th North Carolina Infantry fired into a group of riders returning from a scouting trip in the dark, mistaking them for Union cavalry.
tossups.r: That volley badly wounded their own general, Stonewall Jackson. For 10 points, name this May 1863 battle in Virginia, a victory for Robert E. Lee.

tossups.p: Ernest Hemingway took the title of his 1950 novel _Across the River and into the Trees_ from the last words of a general who was wounded in this battle. That general said, “Let us cross over the river and rest under the shade of the trees.”
tossups.r: That general, Stonewall Jackson, died of pneumonia eight days after he was shot by his own men. For 10 points, name this May 1863 battle won by Robert E. Lee.

tossups.p: On the night of May 1, 1863, two generals sat on empty cracker boxes and planned a daring march after cavalry under Fitzhugh Lee found that the Union right flank was “in the air,” protected by no river or hill.
tossups.r: The next day, Stonewall Jackson’s men marched around that flank and attacked. For 10 points, name this battle in which Robert E. Lee defeated Joseph Hooker.

tossups.p: During this battle, a cannonball struck a porch pillar that a Union commander was leaning against at a brick house, leaving him dazed. Earlier that morning, May 3, he had ordered his troops to give up Hazel Grove, a clearing where Confederate cannons soon set up.
tossups.r: That commander was Joseph Hooker. For 10 points, name this battle in Virginia, Robert E. Lee’s greatest victory.

tossups.p: While the main armies fought to the west during this battle, John Sedgwick’s Union corps captured Marye’s Heights at Fredericksburg, but it was stopped at Salem Church and had to retreat across the Rappahannock River.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this May 1863 battle where Stonewall Jackson was accidentally shot by his own troops, a loss Lee compared to losing his own right arm.

tossups.p: Before this battle, the Union commander sent most of his cavalry under George Stoneman on a raid toward Richmond, which left him with little information about the enemy’s movements.
tossups.r: That commander, Joseph Hooker, was then surprised by Stonewall Jackson’s flank attack. For 10 points, name this May 1863 battle in Virginia.

tossups.p: Before this battle, a Union general reportedly boasted that his plans were perfect and “may God have mercy on General Lee, for I will have none.” That general marched most of his army across the Rappahannock and Rapidan Rivers to get behind Lee, then pulled back to defend.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this May 1863 battle in which Joseph Hooker lost to Robert E. Lee and Stonewall Jackson.

tossups.p: According to the journalist Noah Brooks, Abraham Lincoln paced the room after hearing the news of this battle, crying out, “My God! My God! What will the country say?” The defeated Union army had outnumbered its enemy by more than two to one.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this May 1863 Union defeat, in which Stonewall Jackson was mortally wounded by his own men.

tossups.p: Cavalry general Jeb Stuart temporarily led an infantry corps on May 3, 1863, during this battle, after its commander was wounded and the next general in line, A. P. Hill, was also hurt.
tossups.r: The wounded commander was Stonewall Jackson, who died on May 10. For 10 points, name this battle in which Robert E. Lee defeated Joseph Hooker.

tossups.p: The winning general in this battle fought without James Longstreet, who had taken two divisions to gather supplies near Suffolk in southeastern Virginia. Even so, that general split his outnumbered army twice during this battle and won.
tossups.r: That general was Robert E. Lee. For 10 points, name this May 1863 battle where Lee beat Joseph Hooker.

tossups.p: Historians usually identify this battle as the one that Stephen Crane’s novel _The Red Badge of Courage_ never names, in which the young soldier Henry Fleming runs from the fighting and later returns to his regiment.
tossups.r: In real life, this battle was a victory for Robert E. Lee, though Stonewall Jackson was shot by his own men. For 10 points, name this 1863 battle.

tossups.p: The losing general in this battle disliked his nickname, “Fighting Joe,” which came from a newspaper headline that left out a dash. Months before this battle, Abraham Lincoln’s letter giving him command warned, “What I now ask of you is military success, and I will risk the dictatorship.”
tossups.r: That general was Joseph Hooker. For 10 points, name this May 1863 battle in which Hooker lost to Robert E. Lee.

tossups.p: Late on the afternoon of May 2, 1863, during this battle, deer and rabbits burst out of the woods toward Union soldiers, many of whom were cooking supper. Moments later, thousands of enemy troops came charging out of the trees behind the animals.
tossups.r: That surprise attack by Stonewall Jackson routed Oliver O. Howard’s XI Corps. For 10 points, name this battle, Robert E. Lee’s greatest victory.

tossups.p: This battle’s site is one of four battlefields preserved in the Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania National Military Park. It was named for a large brick house and inn at a crossroads in a scrubby forest called the Wilderness, not for a town.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this May 1863 battle in Virginia, where Robert E. Lee defeated Joseph Hooker.

tossups.p: Historians often call this battle Robert E. Lee’s “perfect battle,” though he lost more than one-fifth of his army in it. Afterward, Lee marched north toward Pennsylvania, and George Meade replaced the losing Union commander just days before the armies met again.
tossups.r: That next meeting came at Gettysburg. For 10 points, name this May 1863 battle where Stonewall Jackson was mortally wounded.

clues.t: Robert E. Lee’s greatest victory, won over Joseph Hooker in Virginia in May 1863
Stonewall Jackson was accidentally shot by his own men there and died on May 10, 1863
Jackson’s surprise march around the Union right flank routed part of Hooker’s army
The win encouraged Lee to invade the North, leading to Gettysburg two months later
Lee was outnumbered more than two to one but split his army twice
Lee said Jackson “has lost his left arm, but I have lost my right”
Jackson’s left arm was amputated, and he died of pneumonia eight days after he was shot
Jackson’s attack late on May 2 routed Oliver O. Howard’s Union XI Corps
Fought in a scrubby forest called the Wilderness, west of Fredericksburg, Virginia
Named for a large brick house and inn at a crossroads, not a town
Hooker crossed the Rappahannock and Rapidan Rivers to get behind Lee, then pulled back to defend
Lee fought without James Longstreet, who had taken two divisions to Suffolk, Virginia
Usually identified as the unnamed battle in Stephen Crane’s _The Red Badge of Courage_
Jackson’s last words: “Let us cross over the river and rest under the shade of the trees”
Ernest Hemingway’s novel _Across the River and into the Trees_ (1950) takes its title from Jackson’s last words
k: across the river and into the trees

trap.title: Chancellorsville or the Wilderness?
trap.body: Chancellorsville (May 1863) and the Battle of the Wilderness (May 1864) were fought in the same tangled Virginia forest, a year apart. Chancellorsville was Lee’s win over Joseph Hooker, where Stonewall Jackson was shot; the Wilderness was Lee against Ulysses S. Grant. The first Battle of Fredericksburg (December 1862) was fought just a few miles east, and Gettysburg came two months after Chancellorsville.
trap.fix: Hooker, Jackson’s flank march, and Jackson’s death mean Chancellorsville. Grant and 1864 mean the Wilderness; Ambrose Burnside’s failed charges in December 1862 mean Fredericksburg.
trap.line: Real answer line: Battle of Chancellorsville (do not accept “Battle of the Wilderness” or “Fredericksburg”)
